topic: Thin films of the all-inorganic perovskites RbxCs1-xPbI3 are made by mixing the small cation Rb+ into CsPbI3, and their optical absorption is measured.

facts.text: On annealing, CsPbI3 films turn into a dark phase with a band gap of 1.73 eV, identified as the three-dimensional perovskite.
The absorption edge moves continuously from 720 nm at x = 0 to 690 nm at x = 0.2.

In the structures optimized by density functional theory, the Pb-I-Pb bond angles approach 180 degrees as the steric radius of the A-site cation grows (about 18 degrees per angstrom), and Rb+ is smaller than Cs+.
The electronic states of the A-site cation lie several eV away from the band edges.

ask: Using E = hc/lambda with hc = 1239.84 eV nm, compute the change of the optical gap from x = 0 to x = 0.2 (in eV) and choose the interpretation. Choose the option in which both the value and the conclusion are correct.

error.reason: 把波长变短（蓝移）当成带隙变小，符号取反。

paper.text: The gap widens: the smaller Rb+ lets the PbI6 octahedra tilt further from the straight Pb-I-Pb geometry, and a larger tilt raises the gap (the calculations had predicted a 40 nm blue shift).
paper.locator: Main text, Rb/Cs experiment: blue shift assigned to the more pronounced octahedral tilt; predicted shift 40 nm

rejected.text: The shift comes from the electronic states of Rb+ itself, which form a new band edge; the tilt of the octahedra plays no part.
rejected.locator: Main text p. 2; Fig. 1b (cation states several eV from the band edges)
